thesis: Evidence quality is strong for the key decision variables: revenue growth, margins, liquidity, cash flow, customer concentration, dilution and the Amazon warrant are all supported by SEC filings or company earnings materials. The main limitations are short public-history depth, billing-location geography that does not equal end demand, and forward uncertainty around Scorpio/Leo adoption and normalized SBC. These limitations affect conviction, not the factual integrity of the current dataset.

evidence.claim: Q2 2026 10-Q directly supports revenue, margins, cash flow, liquidity, share count and customer concentration used across the analysis.
The Q2 earnings release supports the 104% YoY revenue growth, Q3 $540M-$560M revenue guide and approximately 185M diluted-share guide.
The Amazon customer warrant terms are documented in an SEC 8-K rather than inferred from secondary reporting.

The deterministic DCF is generated by the harness from frozen current price, net cash and explicit owner-FCF/share paths; the model does not let the analyst choose discount rate or terminal multiples.

counterevidence: Astera Labs has only a short post-IPO public record and therefore lacks a full-cycle 5-year valuation history.
Revenue geography is based on billing addresses and can overstate China/Singapore/Taiwan end-demand exposure.
Customer identities behind manufacturing-partner billing are not fully observable.
Future Scorpio, Leo X and custom-connectivity economics remain forward-looking.
unknowns: Normalized owner FCF margin through a semiconductor downcycle.
True end-customer concentration after manufacturing partners are mapped to end customers.
Long-run SBC dilution after the current hypergrowth phase.
Scorpio and Leo X multi-generation retention rates.
falsifiers: A later filing that materially revises revenue, cash flow, share count or customer concentration would require re-opening the affected domains.
If billing-location geography is shown to be unrelated to end demand, macro transmission based on geographic revenue should be reduced.
If SBC-adjusted per-share FCF diverges materially from GAAP/OCF trends, RF and valuation normalization should be revisited.
